# 九經字樣

**ID:** KR1j0025
**Custom ID:** ZB1j0022
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V224.4, p295
**Extent:** 1 卷

## Authors / Editors
- 唐玄度 (唐朝) 撰 fl. 833 - 837

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-*juàn* supplementary orthographic dictionary covering 421 graphs not addressed (or differently treated) in Zhāng Shēn's [張參](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E5%8F%83) *Wǔjīng wénzì* [KR1j0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0024). Compiled by Táng Xuándù 唐玄度, *Hànlínyuàn dàizhào* in the Kāichéng era of Wénzōng. Commissioned by imperial decree in Tàihé 7 (833) for the orthographic standardization of the *Kāichéng shíjīng*; co-engraved with the stone *Classics* in 837. Internally arranged in 76 *bù* on the *Wǔjīng wénzì* model.

**Abstract**

The *Jiǔjīng zìyàng* is the orthographic supplement to the *Wǔjīng wénzì*, prepared explicitly for the engraving of the *Kāichéng shíjīng* (837). The text was originally inscribed on stone after the *Nine Classics*; the Jiājìng earthquake of 1555 damaged both books and the *Classics*. The Sìkù compilers used Mǎ Yuēlù's mid-Qing print of a Sòng rubbing as base, but recollated against the surviving stone fragments. Particularly notable is the explicit avoidance of the term *fǎn* 反 in Xuándù's pronunciation glosses, which the Sìkù *tíyào* (in fact, the very same passage cited in the [KR1j0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1j/KR1j0008) *Guǎngyǎ tíyào*) flags as the moment when *fǎn* 反 began to be replaced by *qiè* 切 in Táng phonological notation. Together the *Wǔjīng wénzì* and *Jiǔjīng zìyàng* fix the orthography of the canonical Táng *Classics* — and through their inscription on the *Kāichéng shíjīng*, transmit it without major emendation through the entire imperial period. Dating bracket *notBefore* 833 (imperial commission) to *notAfter* 837 (Kāichéng 2, year of stone-engraving).
